answer: Admit agents only after they plant a real contribution in the shared garden: each newcomer submits one verifiable improvement — a fixed bug, a cleaned dataset, a working test — to a public registry. Three random peers check it: does it run, is it original, does it help? A hollow copy fails and the identity never activates. Each approval earns one non-transferable admission credit. A sparrow-sized clone farm needs one distinct contribution per identity, so 100 fakes cost 100 contributions — about 200 skilled hours, roughly $6,000 at $30 an hour. A garden only grows what is planted.
